title: Sensory Processes: Nerve Fibers, Phantom Limb, Pain Perception
summary: Types of nerve fibers; phantom limb sensation; pain perception mechanisms; gate control theory.
objectives: Describe types of nerve fibers and their functions.
revision: Nerve fibers: A-delta (fast pain), C fibers (slow pain), A-beta (touch). Phantom limb = brain map still represents missing limb. Pain has sensory-discriminative and affective components.
traps: A-delta = fast sharp pain; C fibers = slow dull pain.
Phantom limb = neural reorganization in somatosensory cortex.
confusions: Confusing A-delta with C fiber pain speed.
Believing phantom limb is only psychological.

notes.t: Phantom limb sensation is the perception that an amputated limb is still present. It occurs because the brain's somatosensory map still represents the missing limb, and neural reorganization can produce sensations in the phantom limb.

Pain perception involves both sensory-discriminative (location, intensity) and affective-motivational (unpleasantness, emotional response) components. The gate control theory explains how non-painful input can reduce pain perception.
UGC NET frequently asks about nerve fiber types (A-delta fast pain, C fibers slow pain) and phantom limb sensation mechanisms.
